clue.text: Mildewed Ralph, Shakespearean recruit

definitions.meaning: covered in mould and gone off
Ralph ... is one of the rustics Falstaff musters as a soldier in Henry IV Part 2

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: musty food covered in fungus, and the name of a reluctant conscript pressed into service by Falstaff.

clue.text: We have the legacy of his work, some of which was Caribbean

definitions.text: We have the legacy of his work, some of which was Caribbean

parts.words: We have the legacy of his work, some of which was Caribbean
parts.note: an American novelist whose titles include Legacy and Caribbean

explanation.definitionFit: James Michener wrote the novels Legacy and Caribbean among many sweeping sagas.

clue.text: What one of Cinderella's sisters would have been, provided all three were present

definitions.text: What one of Cinderella's sisters would have been, provided all three were present

parts.words: What one of Cinderella's sisters would have been, provided all three were present
parts.note: with only two sisters a comparative applies; with three, the worst-looking needs the superlative form

explanation.definitionFit: Among three ugly sisters one must be the most unsightly, the superlative degree.

clue.text: Churchyard may be remembered for one of rebellion

definitions.text: Churchyard may be remembered for one of rebellion

parts.words: Churchyard may be remembered for one of rebellion
parts.note: Thomas Churchyard, Elizabethan poet

explanation.definitionFit: Churchyard's 1570 pamphlet on rebellion was titled a discourse, a formal treatise.

clue.text: A Winter's Tale from Midland town?

definitions.meaning: a novella written by the American author Jean ..., not Shakespeare's play
the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands

explanation.walkthrough: The title suggests Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale, but this 'A Winter's Tale' is by Jean Stafford; 'from' links the writer to the place sharing the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The author's surname matches the name of a county town in the Midlands of England.

clue.text: Victim of suffragette from Durham park

definitions.meaning: Mary Richardson slashed Velázquez's painting in the National Gallery in 1914
the painting once hung at Rokeby Park in County Durham, hence its name

explanation.definitionFit: Velázquez's nude was attacked by a suffragette and is named after the Durham house where it once hung.

clue.text: Janus was two

parts.note: the Roman god Janus looked both ways, so the clue completes the phrase for deceitful

explanation.definitionFit: Janus had a pair of visages, making him literally two-faced, the idiom for duplicitous.

clue.text: The gods offered a fine view of the stage from this eminence

definitions.text: The gods offered a fine view of the stage from this eminence

parts.words: The gods offered a fine view of the stage from this eminence
parts.note: the gods are a theatre's highest gallery, and also the Greek deities on their mountain

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek gods watched mortals from their mountain home, as the theatre's top gallery looks down on the stage.

clue.text: But, 1, an honest maid as ever broke bread" (The Merry Wives of Windsor)

definitions.text: But, 1, an honest maid as ever broke bread" (The Merry Wives of Windsor)

parts.words: But, 1, an honest maid as ever broke bread" (The Merry Wives of Windsor)
parts.note: Mistress Quickly's line, where she misuses a word meaning hate when she means protest

explanation.walkthrough: The blank is missing in print; '1' is the pronoun I, and the answer follows it: 'But, I ___, an honest maid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress Quickly's malapropism uses the verb for loathe in place of protest.

clue.text: Revise Eve's age-old quiz for 5's creator

indicators.note: to revise is to rework, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reworks an ancient question set by Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revise' rearranges EVE'S AGE-OLD QUIZ; 5 refers to the painting at 5-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish court painter made the nude at 5-down, so he is its creator.

clue.text: Bentley maid goes to see client, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A housemaid in a Bentley motor car drives off to call on a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bentley' suggests the car, but it is E. C. Bentley, whose Trent's Last Case features the maid Celestine; 'perhaps' rearranges SEE CLIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestine is the French lady's maid in E. C. Bentley's detective novel Trent's Last Case.

clue.text: Location of Lucy Daniels's cat

parts.note: Lucy Daniels's Animal Ark children's series includes a title placing a cat in a church's underground vault

explanation.definitionFit: The Animal Ark book Cat in the Crypt puts its feline beneath a church, in its burial vault.

clue.text: Poetically soon

parts.note: an archaic, verse-flavoured word meaning before long

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a literary, old-fashioned way of saying shortly or before much time passes.

clue.text: Cryptic puzzle solver tragically blinded

parts.note: the Theban king who answered the Sphinx's riddle and later put out his own eyes

explanation.surface: A crossword fan loses their sight in some sad accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles' king of Thebes solved the riddle of the Sphinx and blinded himself on learning his guilt.

clue.text: Stage direction for Dame Ngaio's killer

definitions.meaning: the script instruction telling an actor to come on
Ngaio Marsh's detective novel ... a Murderer gives its killer this word

explanation.definitionFit: It is the theatrical cue to come on stage, and the first word of Ngaio Marsh's title Enter a Murderer.

clue.text: Strange vein seen in Harry Lime's part of Greeneland

definitions.text: in Harry Lime's part of Greeneland

indicators.note: strange tells us the letters are in an odd, unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: An odd vein of character spotted in Graham Greene's villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Lime is the racketeer in Graham Greene's The Third Man, set in post-war Vienna; 'Strange' rearranges VEIN SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Third Man is set in the Austrian capital, so Lime's patch of Greene's fictional world is of that city.

clue.text: You —s! while … you are quarrelling for places the guests must be starved" (Goldsmith)

parts.words: You —s! while … you are quarrelling for places the guests must be starved" (Goldsmith)
parts.note: Hardcastle's rebuke to his servants in She Stoops to Conquer, the blank being a plural insult for dolts

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means blockhead, Hardcastle's insult for his clumsy servants.

clue.text: Greek portico not in amateur fashion

parts.note: someone not amateur is a professional, a pro
style is a fashion or manner

explanation.surface: A Greek porch built in a polished, professional manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostyle describes a classical temple front with a row of columns standing before it.

clue.text: Hesitate on prehistoric track in historic novel

parts.note: to hesitate is to waver
a ley or ley line is a supposed alignment of ancient sites

explanation.surface: Someone dithers while following an ancient path in a period story.
explanation.walkthrough: Ley lines are said to link prehistoric sites; Sir Walter Scott's first historical novel is Waverley.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's 1814 book about the Jacobite rising is the founding example of the historical novel.

clue.text: Give notice for what Booker winner received, they say

indicators.note: they say means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: the Booker winner gets a prize

explanation.surface: Telling someone what the Booker-winning author was awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone formally is to let them know of something.

clue.text: One very close in fielding?

definitions.meaning: close means stingy, so this is a skinflint
Henry Fielding wrote a comedy of this title, adapted from Molière

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cricket fielder very near the bat, but Fielding is the novelist and playwright, whose play The Miser of 1733 is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder is tight-fisted, and Fielding's adaptation of L'Avare carries that title.

clue.text: Runs made by eponymous characters of Le Carré

definitions.meaning: Le Carré's novel Single & Single is named after its father-and-son characters

explanation.definitionFit: A single in cricket scores one run, and the Singles are the family in Le Carré's Single & Single.

clue.text: Writer reveals the Spanish in alliance

indicators.note: in means the Spanish article goes inside the alliance

parts.note: a bloc is a group of allied nations
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An author exposes Spain's role in a political pact.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilaire Belloc was an Anglo-French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc wrote essays, verse and the Cautionary Tales.

clue.text: Out of the medium, and fast

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of
the press is the news medium

explanation.surface: A psychic leaves a seance and starts fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: An express train or delivery is a rapid one.

clue.text: Stopover in Bourget — a perfect weekend

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: A break on a journey at Le Bourget, making a perfect weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: Bourget suggests the Paris airport, but Paul Bourget wrote the novel L'Étape.
explanation.definitionFit: An étape is a stage or halting place on a journey.

clue.text: German town has points for ascetic sectarians

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A town in Germany is pointed out as home to a strict religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: These were a Jewish sect of the Second Temple period known for austere communal living.

clue.text: "Iolanthe was the life and soul of Fairyland", she said

definitions.text: "Iolanthe was the life and soul of Fairyland", she said

parts.words: "Iolanthe was the life and soul of Fairyland", she said
parts.note: a line spoken by one of the fairies at the start of Gilbert and Sullivan's opera Iolanthe

explanation.definitionFit: In Gilbert and Sullivan's opera the fairy Leila laments the banished Iolanthe with this line.

clue.text: Camilla, thoughtful, walked alone into the garden" (Fanny Burney)

definitions.text: Camilla, thoughtful, walked alone into the garden" (Fanny Burney)

parts.words: Camilla, thoughtful, walked alone into the garden" (Fanny Burney)
parts.note: a quotation from Burney's novel Camilla with an adverb missing before 'thoughtful'

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has lost its blank; the missing word goes between 'Camilla,' and 'thoughtful'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adverb means out of the ordinary, describing how pensive the heroine was.

clue.text: Den craze could produce legless bookcase

indicators.note: could produce suggests the letters can be worked into something new

explanation.surface: A passion for home dens results in furniture with no legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A credenza is a sideboard or low cabinet, often used as a bookcase without legs.

clue.text: Norfolk city diocese hosts garden party on Bastille Day

definitions.text: hosts garden party on Bastille Day

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in the Fens, placed in Norfolk by the setter
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A cathedral diocese holds a summer fete on the French national holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is in fact in Cambridgeshire, near Norfolk. The Élysée Palace, the French president's residence, holds a garden party on 14 July.
explanation.definitionFit: The French presidential palace traditionally hosts a reception in its grounds on the national day.
